problem_definition: Test whether a future candidate can maintain and update bounded self/other latent state under partial observability, then use that latent state to predict and act under heldout partner dynamics, partner shifts, counterfactual partner responses, and interventions.

target_conditions.description: Candidate must maintain distinguishable self_state and other_state representations or auditable state partitions.
Other-state updates must be derived from observed partner behavior and interaction history, not partner ID, labels, filenames, fixture names, or explicit preference tokens.
Candidate must predict partner behavior before observation under changed context, partner policy shift, or preference shift.
Candidate behavior must adapt after a partner policy or preference shift using new evidence.
Candidate action selection must depend on inferred other_state rather than static partner lookup.
Future evidence must expose state snapshots, hashes, deltas, update events, or equivalent auditable latent-update records.
Replay must recompute behavior from serialized_state plus observation, not only compare trace hashes.
A real ablation disabling the social-latent update path must fail or degrade the claimed behavior under rerun episodes.

candidate_success_ordering: define faithful non-mechanism baselines and access rights first
freeze heldout and counterfactual partner dynamics
freeze leakage positive-control and no-signal negative-control cases
define candidate metrics only after baseline collapse channels are explicit
treat strongest faithful baseline tie as negative evidence, not as a repair TODO
mechanism_claim_ceiling_for_future_task: bounded offline mechanism-proxy evidence for the named future task only, if and only if all baseline, ablation, replay, leakage, provenance, and claim-ceiling gates pass
current_task_claim_ceiling: problem-definition reset and future task-card recommendation only
